label: PF Backlog 602
title: EDP-21: MemoryRepository behind the 8 memory types; PG metadata + object payloads; FTS then pgvector; ACL-filtered retrieval + leakage tests

decisions.note: Gate 1: EDP-21 design approved. RLS via BindTenant session GUC; down migration additive/non-destructive; dimension 1536; acl_scope enum; FTS-first with 0.7/0.3 hybrid; deterministic tiebreak.
Gate 2: memory repository (8 types/FTS/hybrid/ACL) delivered (038718cfdba8); follow-ups deferred.

brief.problem: Memory storage is scattered and unindexed, with no ACL-safe hybrid search across the 8 memory types.
brief.what_adds: A unified MemoryRepository with PG metadata, object payloads, FTS+pgvector search, and server-side ACL filtering.
brief.why: Enterprise retrieval needs secure, fast, consistent memory access.
brief.who_feels: Developers and admins querying agent memory; security reviewers.

objective: Implement MemoryRepository behind the 8 memory types with PostgreSQL metadata + object payloads, FTS-first hybrid search (pgvector when available), and server-side ACL filtering proven by leakage tests.
acceptance_criteria: All eight memory types (raw_evidence, semantic, episodic, decision, procedural, failure, policy, working) are accepted and persisted by MemoryStore with tenant_id/project/source/owner/kind/acl_scope/content and optional object_ref; unknown kinds fail closed.

Migration 0015 adds content/source/owner, a generated tsvector + GIN index, ACL indexes, and an optional pgvector embedding column (created only when the vector extension is available, so the migration never fails on a stock PostgreSQL).

MemoryStore.Search runs full-text search first (websearch_to_tsquery + ts_rank with a deterministic order) and merges vector similarity when an embedding is supplied AND pgvector is available; otherwise it degrades to FTS-only, never erroring on a missing extension.

ACL filtering is server-side in SQL: tenant (RLS plus explicit guard), project, source, kinds, and user (private entries only for their owner); a negative test proves zero cross-tenant, cross-project, cross-source and cross-user leakage.
The /memory API stays backward compatible (existing fields and kind-as-query behaviour) while accepting optional content/source/owner/acl_scope/embedding and q/kinds/user/k parameters.
Verification: Go integration tests against PostgreSQL (8 types, FTS ranking, hybrid/vector degradation, ACL leakage negatives) plus unit tests; precheck PASS.
in_scope: Memory schema/migration (content, source, owner, FTS, optional vector).
MemoryStore 8 types + FTS/hybrid search + ACL filters + API backward compatibility.
approach: 1) migrations/0015_memory_repository.up.sql: ALTER TABLE memory + tsvector/GIN + optional vector column/index. 2) datastore.MemoryEntry/MemoryScope: content/source/owner/score/kinds/user/vector. 3) MemoryStore: validate 8 kinds, persist metadata, FTS-first search, optional hybrid, SQL ACL predicates. 4) edpsvc /memory accepts new fields/params without breaking existing clients. 5) Go integration tests with PG (leakage + ranking) and unit tests.
verification: PARTIAL: memory table + MemoryStore (Put/Get/Delete/scoped Search) + /memory API merged. REMAINING: 8 memory types + FTS/pgvector + leakage tests.
risks: pgvector absent in stock PG: degradation is FTS-only (documented; hybrid tested when available).
ACL predicate mistakes could leak: covered by four negative leakage tests.
Backward compatibility: existing POST/GET fields retained; kind-as-query kept when q is absent.
rollback: Feature-flag repository behind MemoryRepository; fall back to legacy agent_memory path; schema migrations are additive.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Wrap core/agent_memory.py and core/memory_api.py behind a new MemoryRepository interface; store PG metadata + object-store payloads reusing EDP-15 stored_objects; FTS (tsvector) first, pgvector fallback; ACL filter via tenant-context (EDP-09).
conflict_findings: Concurrent risk with BI-PF-1312 on storage.py split — sequence after it
BI-PF-1314 touches memory read paths for tuning — coordinate later
duplication_findings: core/agent_memory.py already implements in-memory/partial memory types — reuse, do not rebuild
Check BI-PF-1312 for overlapping checkpoint/evidence storage rules
analysis.rationale: Memory is a core capability; existing agent_memory/memory_api give a solid base to extend behind a repository abstraction with ACL-filtered, hybrid search.
assumptions: PostgreSQL with pgvector optional; FTS always available
Object payloads fit EDP-15 artifact/object-store pattern
Existing memory API contracts stay backward compatible
risks: pgvector not available in all deployment targets — need FTS-only fallback
ACL leakage risk if filters applied post-query
8 memory types may have divergent schemas
missing_info: Which 8 memory types are canonical — confirm list from roadmap section
Payload size limits for object-store offload

context_review.reason: Existing memory modules and storage roadmap give enough to implement; a few schema/target confirmations needed.

api_impact.reason: Memory API gains optional content/source/owner/acl_scope/embedding and search params while staying compatible.
